correctness.rationale: Conditioning a specified vertex to be isolated requires the other n-1 iid locations to fall on its one complementary circular arc of length L=1-2r. Pair separation on this arc has triangular density 2(L-s)/L²; because L<1-r, circular edges cannot arise by the long-way-around distance, so conditional edge probability is 2r/L-(r/L)² for r<=1/3 and 1 for r>=1/3. Mixed first moment then yields Cov(I,E)=binom(n,2)L^{n-1}[(n-2)q(r)-2nr] for all n>=2 and 0<r<1/2. For r<=1/3 its sign is a concave quadratic -8nr²+(3n+10)r-4; for r>=1/3 the sign is n(1-2r)-2. At n<=5 sign is negative; for n>=6 the exactly computed roots r_-(n) and r_+(n) bound the unique positive window. Independently checked symbolic algebra and n=6,r=3/10 giving exactly 72/3125; boundary n=6 roots 1/4 and 1/3. This finite-n identity has a direct analytic proof, separate from sampled discrete grids.
